key_insight: Post-selection and entanglement are separate resources: post-selection can boost weak Bell-type correlations, but entanglement is required to surpass the separable PPS bounds.
engineering_relevance: The result suggests hybrid quantum sensing and information protocols can gain extra signal strength by combining weak-measurement post-selection with entangled states.
method: Analyze anomalous weak values of the CHSH operator in pre- and post-selected ensembles.
Compare three bound settings: unrestricted boundary states, one separable boundary state, and both boundary states separable.
Optimize both the measurement choice and the post-selected states to find maximal weak-value violations and entanglement witness power.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytic optimization results showing the largest correlations occur when post-selection and entanglement are combined, with the excess over separable bounds tracking concurrence.
watch_item: The strongest witness performance is state-adapted and idealized, so practical noise, imperfect post-selection, and measurement misalignment may reduce the observed advantage.
paper_title: Quantum nonlocal correlations of anomalous weak values
